subject: general
question: Which of the following rivers is associated with National Waterway 10 (NW-10)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amba river**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Waterway 10 (NW-10)** is one of the recognized inland waterways in India under the National Waterways Act, 2016. It is established to promote inland navigation and transport.
 
• The **Amba River** is located in the state of Maharashtra, and it flows near Dharamtar Port, which serves as a crucial point for inland water transport.
 
• NW-10 covers the stretch of the **Amba River from Dharamtar Port to its confluence with the Arabian Sea**. This stretch is significant for trade and transport activities.
 
• The recognition of NW-10 under the **National Waterways Act, 2016** aims to enhance the utilization of inland waterways for reducing transportation costs and improving logistics efficiency.
 
• Other rivers mentioned in the options, such as the **Brahmaputra**, **Chambal**, and **Yamuna**, are associated with different national waterways like NW-2, NW-3, and NW-1 respectively. They are not part of NW-10.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Waterways Act, 2016:**

 
 
• India passed the **National Waterways Act** in **March 2016**, identifying 111 inland waterways as national waterways.
 
• The Act aims to promote inland water transport for trade, tourism, and efficient logistics.
 
 
 
• **Amba River:**
 
 
• The **Amba River** flows through the Raigad district of Maharashtra.
 
• Its proximity to Dharamtar Port has made it crucial for inland water transport activities.
 
 
 
• **National Waterway 1 (NW-1):**
 
 
• NW-1 is one of the longest waterways in India, covering the stretch of the **Ganga River** from Allahabad to Haldia.
 
• This waterway is significant for trade and transport across northern and eastern India.
 
 
 
• **National Waterway 2 (NW-2):**
 
 
• NW-2 covers the stretch of the **Brahmaputra River** from Dhubri to Sadiya in Assam.
 
• It plays a vital role in connecting the northeastern region of India with the rest of the country.
 
 
 
• **National Waterway 3 (NW-3):**
 
 
• NW-3 is located in Kerala and covers the stretch from Kollam to Kottapuram, including the Champakara and Udyogmandal canals.
 
• It facilitates transport and trade activities in the southern state of Kerala.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inland Waterways:**

 
 
• India’s waterways are divided into national and state waterways. National waterways are regulated by the central government, while state waterways are managed by respective states.
 
• Inland waterways are eco-friendly and cost-effective methods of transportation compared to road and rail transport.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Inland Water Transport:**
 
 
• It reduces **carbon emissions** and contributes to environmental sustainability.
 
• It lowers transportation costs, especially for bulk cargo and goods.
 
• It promotes **regional development** by improving connectivity and logistics efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Dharamtar Port:**
 
 
• Located on the Amba River, Dharamtar Port is a vital inland port that supports logistics and trade activities.
 
• It contributes significantly to the economic activities of Maharashtra and neighboring regions.
